country.name: Ecuador
country.tagline: Vineyards on the equator, from the Andes above Quito to the limestone coast of Guayas.

stats.note: Three producers reported as of 2022 (Primicias); no national statistics found.

country.overview:
Ecuador's wine scene is tiny and improbable: vines growing almost exactly on the equator, without seasons. As of 2022 a Spanish journalist counted three producers. Chaupi Estancia, the oldest, has grown grapes for about 30 years at Yaruquí, near Quito, at about 2,400 m and only 10 km from the equator line, making Palomino, a Chardonnay and Viognier blend, Pinot Noir and experimental blends. Dos Hemisferios, the best known, began as a table-grape grower in San Miguel del Morro on the coast of Guayas and turned to wine from 2004, with limestone soils swept by sea breezes; its first wine, Paradoja (Cabernet Sauvignon and Malbec), came from the 2006 harvest. Viña del Guayacán, founded in 2017 at Zapotillo in Loja near the Peruvian border, makes small lots of Cabernet Sauvignon and Chardonnay.

With no winter, vines can be harvested twice a year, but they age fast and rarely live beyond about 25 years. There is no appellation system.

history.title: Chaupi Estancia
history.text: Chaupi Estancia begins growing vines at Yaruquí near Quito, at about 2,400 m on the equator.

history.title: Dos Hemisferios
history.text: A table-grape grower in coastal Guayas turns to wine; its first wine, Paradoja, comes from the 2006 harvest.

history.title: Viña del Guayacán
history.text: A third winery is founded at Zapotillo, Loja, near the Peruvian border.

country.classification: Ecuador has no wine appellation system.
country.climate_soils: Equatorial: no seasons, so vines are pruned to give up to two harvests a year. The Andes give cool nights at 2,400 m near Quito; the Guayas coast is warm but cooled by the Humboldt Current, with limestone soils.

grapes.name: Chardonnay, Viognier, Palomino
grapes.note: Whites from the highlands and coast.

sources.title: Primicias, Tres viñedos en la mitad del mundo (Ignacio Medina, April 2022)

sites.name: Dos Hemisferios
sites.text: Ecuador's best-known winery, in San Miguel del Morro, Guayas, near the Pacific. A former table-grape grower, it made its first wine, Paradoja, from the 2006 harvest; sea breezes and limestone soils, plus two harvests a year, shape its reds and whites.

sites.name: Chaupi Estancia, Yaruquí
sites.text: Ecuador's oldest wine estate, planted about 30 years ago at Yaruquí in the Quito district, at about 2,400 m and roughly 10 km from the equator. It makes Palomino, a Chardonnay and Viognier blend and Pinot Noir in a land of 'eternal spring'.
